name: Пропущен be (I am a student, I am 20, I will be happy)
text_ru: В английском предложении всегда есть глагол: где по-русски его нет («я студент», «мне 20 лет»), ставим am / is / are (I am a student, I am 20, I will be happy).
text_en: Every English sentence needs a verb: use am / is / are where Russian has none (I am a student, I am 20, I will be happy).
wrong: I student. I have 20 years.
right: I am a student. I am 20 years old.

name: am, is или are
text_ru: С I используется am, с he / she / it — is, с we / you / they — are.
text_en: Use am with I, is with he / she / it, and are with we / you / they.
wrong: She are my friend.
right: She is my friend.

name: Лишний be перед смысловым глаголом
text_ru: Если в предложении уже есть смысловой глагол (agree, like, live), am / is / are не нужен: I agree, I like pizza.
text_en: Do not add am / is / are before a main verb: I agree, I like pizza.
wrong: I am agree. I am like pizza.
right: I agree. I like pizza.

name: Множественное число: -s / -es / -ies и особые формы (children, men)
text_ru: Множественное число образуется с -s (brothers), после s, x, ch, sh — с -es (boxes), y после согласной меняется на -ies (cities); у некоторых слов особая форма (children, men, people).
text_en: Plurals take -s, -es after s / x / ch / sh, and -ies after a consonant + y; some are irregular (children, men, people).
wrong: I have two brother. Three citys. Two childs.
right: I have two brothers. Three cities. Two children.

name: a / an перед исчисляемым в ед. ч.; an перед гласным звуком; не перед мн. ч.
text_ru: Перед исчисляемым существительным в единственном числе нужен артикль a, перед гласным звуком — an (a dog, an apple); с множественным числом a не ставится.
text_en: A singular countable noun needs a, or an before a vowel sound (a dog, an apple); a is not used with plurals.
wrong: I have dog and a apple.
right: I have a dog and an apple.

name: Личные местоимения: I / me, he / she / it; подлежащее it нельзя пропускать
text_ru: Перед глаголом — I, he, she, it, we, they, после глагола — me, him, her, us, them; подлежащее не пропускается, о погоде и предметах говорим it (It is raining).
text_en: Use I / he / she / we / they before the verb and me / him / her / us / them after it; a sentence needs a subject, so say It is raining.
wrong: He loves she. Is raining.
right: He loves her. It is raining.

name: Притяжательные: my, his, her, 's
text_ru: «Мой, его, её» — my, his, her: his, если владелец мужчина, her — если женщина; «папина машина» — my father's car.
text_en: Use my, his, her before a noun: his for a male owner, her for a female owner; use 's for a person's things (my father's car).
wrong: This is me brother. I love mine parents.
right: This is my brother. I love my parents.

name: this / that — ед. ч., these / those — мн. ч.
text_ru: This / that — для одного предмета, these / those — для нескольких (These are my friends).
text_en: Use this / that with one thing and these / those with several (These are my friends).
wrong: This are my friends.
right: These are my friends.

name: -s у глагола после he / she / it, somebody, everybody (has, has got, goes, studies)
text_ru: В Present Simple после he, she, it (а также somebody, everybody) к глаголу добавляется -s: she works, he goes, she studies, she has, she has got.
text_en: In the Present Simple add -s after he / she / it (and somebody, everybody): she works, he goes, she studies, she has, she has got.
wrong: She work and have a car.
right: She works and has a car.

name: Лишнее -s после I / you / we / they
text_ru: После I, you, we, they глагол в Present Simple стоит без -s: they work.
text_en: After I / you / we / they the verb has no -s: they work.
wrong: They works in a bank.
right: They work in a bank.

name: Отрицание и вопрос без do / does
text_ru: Отрицание и вопрос в Present Simple строятся с do / does: I don't like coffee; Do you like tea?
text_en: Present Simple negatives and questions need do / does: I don't like coffee; Do you like tea?
wrong: I not like coffee. You like tea?
right: I don't like coffee. Do you like tea?

name: do или does, don't или doesn't
text_ru: С he, she, it используется does / doesn't, с остальными — do / don't.
text_en: Use does / doesn't with he / she / it and do / don't with the others.
wrong: She don't like coffee. Do she like tea?
right: She doesn't like coffee. Does she like tea?

name: После does / doesn't глагол без -s
text_ru: -s уже есть в does, поэтому смысловой глагол после does / doesn't стоит без -s: She doesn't like it; Does she like it?
text_en: Does already carries the -s, so the main verb has none: She doesn't like it; Does she like it?
wrong: She doesn't likes coffee. Does she likes tea?
right: She doesn't like coffee. Does she like tea?

name: Наречие частоты — перед глаголом, но после be
text_ru: Наречия частоты (always, usually, often, never) стоят перед смысловым глаголом, но после am / is / are: I usually drink tea; She is never late.
text_en: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb but after am / is / are: I usually drink tea; She is never late.
wrong: I drink usually tea. She never is late.
right: I usually drink tea. She is never late.

name: at / on / in со временем; без предлога перед next, last, every, this
text_ru: At — с часами (at 5), on — с днями и датами (on Monday), in — с месяцами, годами и временами года (in July); перед next, last, every, this предлог не нужен.
text_en: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, in for months, years and seasons; no preposition before next, last, every, this.
wrong: See you in Monday at 5. I will go on next week.
right: See you on Monday at 5. I will go next week.

name: in / on / at, at home, next to, go to (направление)
text_ru: In — внутри, on — на поверхности, at — в точке (at home, at school); направление — to (go to school), но go home без to.
text_en: Use in for inside, on for surfaces, at for points (at home); use to for direction (go to school), but say go home.
wrong: The book is in the table. I go in school.
right: The book is on the table. I go to school.

name: С be (am / is / are, was / were, Continuous) вопрос и отрицание без do
text_ru: С am / is / are и was / were (в том числе в Continuous) do не нужен: в вопросе be ставится перед подлежащим, в отрицании добавляется not (Are you hungry? I am not working).
text_en: With be (am / is / are, was / were, also in Continuous tenses) do is not used: put be before the subject in questions and add not in negatives.
wrong: Do you are hungry? I don't working now.
right: Are you hungry? I am not working now.

name: В вопросе вспомогательный глагол перед подлежащим
text_ru: В английском вопросе вспомогательный глагол (do, is, are, can...) стоит перед подлежащим: Where do you live? Is there a cafe here?
text_en: In questions the auxiliary (do, is, can...) comes before the subject: Where do you live? Is there a cafe here?
wrong: Where you live? There is a cafe here?
right: Where do you live? Is there a cafe here?

name: Краткий ответ — вспомогательным глаголом
text_ru: В кратком ответе повторяем вспомогательный глагол из вопроса, а не смысловой: Do you like tea? — Yes, I do.
text_en: Short answers repeat the auxiliary from the question, not the main verb: Do you like tea? — Yes, I do.
wrong: Do you like tea? — Yes, I like.
right: Do you like tea? — Yes, I do.

name: После can, could, must, should, might, will — глагол без to и без -s
text_ru: После can, could, must, should, might, will глагол стоит в начальной форме без to и без -s: I can swim, she will go.
text_en: After can, could, must, should, might and will use the base verb without to or -s: I can swim, she will go.
wrong: I can to swim. She will goes there.
right: I can swim. She will go there.

name: Отрицание и вопрос с can, could, should, will, must — без do / did
text_ru: Модальные глаголы сами образуют отрицание и вопрос, do / did с ними не нужен: I can't swim; Could you come?
text_en: Modal verbs form negatives and questions without do / did: I can't swim; Could you come?
wrong: I don't can swim. Did you could come?
right: I can't swim. Could you come?

name: После enjoy, finish, mind — глагол с -ing; после like, love, hate — -ing или to
text_ru: После enjoy, finish, mind глагол стоит только с -ing (I enjoy dancing); после like, love, hate можно и -ing, и to (I like swimming / I like to swim), но не просто глагол (I like swim).
text_en: After enjoy, finish and mind use only the -ing form (I enjoy dancing); after like, love and hate use -ing or to (I like swimming / I like to swim), but not the bare verb.
wrong: I like swim. I enjoy to dance.
right: I like swimming. I enjoy dancing.

name: Форма Present Continuous: am / is / are + глагол с -ing (пропущен be или -ing)
text_ru: Present Continuous = am / is / are + глагол с -ing: I am walking, they are running.
text_en: The Present Continuous is am / is / are + verb-ing: I am walking, they are running.
wrong: I walking in the park. They is run.
right: I am walking in the park. They are running.

name: Выбор времени: сейчас — Present Continuous, регулярно — Present Simple
text_ru: О том, что происходит прямо сейчас, говорим в Present Continuous (I am walking now), а о привычках и регулярных действиях — в Present Simple (I get up at 7 every day).
text_en: Use the Present Continuous for what is happening now and the Present Simple for habits and routines (I get up at 7 every day).
wrong: I walk with my friend now. I am getting up at 7 every day.
right: I am walking with my friend now. I get up at 7 every day.

name: is / was — для одного, are / were — для нескольких
text_ru: There is / was — для одного предмета или неисчисляемого существительного, there are / were — для нескольких: There are two dogs.
text_en: Use there is / was with one thing or an uncountable noun and there are / were with plurals: There are two dogs.
wrong: There is two dogs. There was many people.
right: There are two dogs. There were many people.

name: Пропущено there (калька «В парке есть...»)
text_ru: «Где-то есть что-то» по-английски начинается с there is / there are, а место ставится в конец: There is a dog in the park.
text_en: To say that something exists somewhere, start with there is / there are and put the place at the end: There is a dog in the park.
wrong: In the park is a dog. In the park have many trees.
right: There is a dog in the park. There are many trees in the park.

name: О прошлом (yesterday, last, ago) — Past Simple; -ed у правильных глаголов
text_ru: О законченных действиях в прошлом (yesterday, last week, ago) говорим в Past Simple: к правильным глаголам добавляется -ed (played, visited).
text_en: Use the Past Simple for finished past actions (yesterday, last week, ago); regular verbs take -ed (played, visited).
wrong: Yesterday I play tennis and go home.
right: Yesterday I played tennis and went home.

name: Неправильные глаголы: went, bought, saw (без -ed, не третья форма)
text_ru: У неправильных глаголов своя форма прошедшего времени — вторая форма из таблицы (go — went, see — saw, buy — bought), -ed не добавляется.
text_en: Irregular verbs have their own past form, the second form in the table (go — went, see — saw, buy — bought), not -ed.
wrong: I goed to the park and seen him.
right: I went to the park and saw him.

name: Отрицание и вопрос — did / didn't + начальная форма
text_ru: Отрицание и вопрос в Past Simple — did / didn't + глагол в начальной форме: I didn't go; Where did you go?
text_en: Past Simple negatives and questions use did / didn't + the base verb: I didn't go; Where did you go?
wrong: I didn't went there. Where you went?
right: I didn't go there. Where did you go?

name: was или were
text_ru: С I, he, she, it используется was, с you, we, they — were.
text_en: Use was with I / he / she / it and were with you / we / they.
wrong: They was at home. I were tired.
right: They were at home. I was tired.

name: some — в утверждении; any, anything, anybody — в отрицании и вопросе
text_ru: Some (something, somebody) — в утвердительных предложениях, any (anything, anybody) — в отрицаниях и вопросах; в просьбах и предложениях тоже some (Would you like some tea?).
text_en: Use some (something, somebody) in positive sentences and any (anything, anybody) in negatives and questions; offers and requests also use some (Would you like some tea?).
wrong: I don't have some sugar. I didn't see something.
right: I don't have any sugar. I didn't see anything.

name: Выбор слова по исчисляемости: many / much, few / little, How many / How much
text_ru: С исчисляемыми (friends, apples) — many, few, How many, с неисчисляемыми (money, time) — much, little, How much; a lot of подходит для обоих.
text_en: Use many / few / How many with countable nouns and much / little / How much with uncountable nouns; a lot of works with both.
wrong: I don't have many money. How much apples? I have a lot friends.
right: I don't have much money. How many apples? I have a lot of friends.

name: Неисчисляемые (advice, information, news, hair): без -s, без a, глагол в ед. ч.
text_ru: Некоторые слова в английском неисчисляемые (advice, information, news, money, hair): у них нет -s и артикля a, а глагол стоит в единственном числе (The news is good).
text_en: Some nouns are uncountable (advice, information, news, hair): no -s, no a, and a singular verb (The news is good).
wrong: He gave me an advice. The news are good.
right: He gave me some advice. The news is good.

name: -er / -est или more / most; better, the best; без двойного сравнения
text_ru: Короткие прилагательные получают -er / -est (cheaper, the biggest), длинные — more / most (more beautiful); good — better — the best, bad — worse — the worst; more и -er вместе не используются.
text_en: Short adjectives take -er / -est, long ones take more / most; good — better — the best, bad — worse — the worst; never use more together with -er.
wrong: It is more cheap and more bigger. This is gooder.
right: It is cheaper and bigger. This is better.

name: После сравнительной степени — than, перед превосходной — the
text_ru: После сравнительной степени ставим than (taller than me), а перед превосходной — the (the best student).
text_en: Use than after a comparative (taller than me) and the before a superlative (the best student).
wrong: He is taller then me. She is best student.
right: He is taller than me. She is the best student.

name: am / is / are + going to + глагол
text_ru: Планы на будущее: am / is / are + going to + глагол в начальной форме (I am going to visit my aunt).
text_en: For plans use am / is / are + going to + the base verb (I am going to visit my aunt).
wrong: I going visit my aunt.
right: I am going to visit my aunt.

name: have / has + третья форма; вопрос — Have you...?, без do
text_ru: Present Perfect = have / has + третья форма глагола (I have seen, she has gone); в вопросе have / has ставится перед подлежащим, do не нужен.
text_en: The Present Perfect is have / has + past participle (I have seen, she has gone); questions start with have / has, not do.
wrong: I seen this film. She have went. Do you have seen it?
right: I have seen this film. She has gone. Have you seen it?

name: Один союз на два предложения (не because... so, although... but)
text_ru: Два предложения соединяет один союз: Because I was tired, I went home (или I was tired, so I went home).
text_en: One conjunction links two clauses: Because I was tired, I went home, or I was tired, so I went home.
wrong: Because I was tired, so I went home.
right: Because I was tired, I went home.

name: Перед существительным — because of
text_ru: Because ставится перед предложением (because it rained), а перед существительным — because of (because of the rain).
text_en: Use because before a clause and because of before a noun (because of the rain).
wrong: We stayed at home because the rain.
right: We stayed at home because of the rain.

name: the — когда понятно, о чём речь, и с единственными (the sun)
text_ru: The ставим, когда понятно, о каком предмете речь (его уже упоминали или он единственный): The film was good; The sun is shining.
text_en: Use the when it is clear which thing you mean or when it is unique: The film was good; The sun is shining.
wrong: I saw a film. A film was good. Sun is shining.
right: I saw a film. The film was good. The sun is shining.

name: Без артикля: о чём-то в общем, имена и города, have breakfast, by bus
text_ru: Артикль не нужен, когда говорим о чём-то в общем (I like dogs), с именами и городами (Moscow) и в выражениях have breakfast, go to bed, by bus.
text_en: Use no article for things in general (I like dogs), with names and cities (Moscow) and in phrases like have breakfast, go to bed, by bus.
wrong: I like the dogs. I live in the Moscow.
right: I like dogs. I live in Moscow.

name: Решение сейчас — will, план — going to, договорённость — Present Continuous
text_ru: Решение в момент речи, обещание или предложение помощи — will (I'll close the window); заранее продуманный план — going to; договорённость на конкретное время — Present Continuous (I'm meeting my friend at six).
text_en: Use will for decisions made now, promises and offers, going to for plans, and the Present Continuous for fixed arrangements (I'm meeting my friend at six).
wrong: It's cold. — I close the window. I meet my friend tomorrow at six.
right: It's cold. — I'll close the window. I'm meeting my friend tomorrow at six.

name: was / were + глагол с -ing
text_ru: Past Continuous = was / were + глагол с -ing: I was watching TV, they were playing.
text_en: The Past Continuous is was / were + verb-ing: I was watching TV, they were playing.
wrong: At 8 I watching TV. They was playing.
right: At 8 I was watching TV. They were playing.

name: Длительное действие (фон) — Continuous, короткое (прервало) — Simple
text_ru: Длительное действие в прошлом (фон) — Past Continuous, короткое действие, которое его прервало, — Past Simple: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
text_en: Use the Past Continuous for the longer background action and the Past Simple for the short action that interrupted it: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
wrong: I watched TV when the phone was ringing.
right: I was watching TV when the phone rang.

name: ever, never, already, just, yet: место и выбор
text_ru: Ever, never, just, already стоят между have и третьей формой (I have never been there); yet — в конце отрицаний и вопросов (I haven't finished yet).
text_en: Ever, never, just and already go between have and the participle (I have never been there); yet goes at the end of negatives and questions (I haven't finished yet).
wrong: I have been never there. I haven't finished already.
right: I have never been there. I haven't finished yet.

name: for / since, How long — Present Perfect, а не Present Simple
text_ru: Если действие началось в прошлом и продолжается сейчас (for, since, How long), нужен Present Perfect, а не Present Simple: I have known him since 2018; for — период, since — момент начала.
text_en: For situations that started in the past and continue now (for, since, How long) use the Present Perfect: I have known him since 2018; for + period, since + starting point.
wrong: I know him since 2018. How long do you live here?
right: I have known him since 2018. How long have you lived here?

name: Указано время в прошлом или When — Past Simple; опыт без времени — Present Perfect
text_ru: Если указано, когда это было (in 2019, yesterday), или вопрос начинается с When, нужен Past Simple; опыт без указания времени — Present Perfect (I have been to Rome).
text_en: With a finished time (in 2019, yesterday) or a When question use the Past Simple; for experience without a time use the Present Perfect (I have been to Rome).
wrong: I have visited Rome in 2019. When have you arrived?
right: I visited Rome in 2019. When did you arrive?

name: enough — после прилагательного, перед существительным; too — «слишком», не «очень»
text_ru: Enough стоит после прилагательного (big enough) и перед существительным (enough money); too значит «слишком» (это плохо), а «очень» — very.
text_en: Enough goes after adjectives (big enough) and before nouns (enough money); too means more than is good, so use very to say a lot.
wrong: It is not enough big. Your dress is too beautiful!
right: It is not big enough. Your dress is very beautiful!

name: to + глагол: после want, decide, hope, после прилагательных, для цели; want someone to
text_ru: После want, decide, hope, после прилагательных (easy to learn) и для цели («чтобы») используется to + глагол; «хочу, чтобы ты пришёл» — I want you to come.
text_en: Use to + verb after want, decide, hope, after adjectives (easy to learn) and to express purpose; say I want you to come, not I want that you come.
wrong: I want go. I came for learn English. I want that you come.
right: I want to go. I came to learn English. I want you to come.

name: После предлога (in, at, before, look forward to) — глагол с -ing
text_ru: После предлога глагол всегда с -ing: interested in learning, before going; в look forward to слово to — тоже предлог (look forward to hearing).
text_en: After a preposition use the -ing form: interested in learning, before going; in look forward to, to is a preposition (look forward to hearing).
wrong: I am interested in learn. I look forward to hear from you.
right: I am interested in learning. I look forward to hearing from you.

name: has to после he / she / it; в прошлом — had to; отрицание и вопрос — через do
text_ru: С he, she, it — has to; у must нет прошедшего времени, вместо него had to; отрицание и вопрос с have to строятся через do (I don't have to go; Do you have to work?).
text_en: Use has to with he / she / it; the past of must is had to; have to forms negatives and questions with do (I don't have to go; Do you have to work?).
wrong: She have to work. Yesterday I must go. I haven't to go.
right: She has to work. Yesterday I had to go. I don't have to go.

name: mustn't — нельзя, don't have to — не обязательно
text_ru: Mustn't значит «нельзя», а don't have to — «не обязательно, не нужно».
text_en: Mustn't means it is not allowed; don't have to means it is not necessary.
wrong: You mustn't come tomorrow, it's a holiday.
right: You don't have to come tomorrow, it's a holiday.

name: who — о людях, which / that — о предметах (не what); без лишнего it
text_ru: О людях — who, о предметах — which или that (не what); слово, к которому относится придаточное, в нём не повторяется: the book that I read.
text_en: Use who for people and which / that for things (not what), and do not repeat the noun with it: the book that I read.
wrong: The man which lives here. The book what I read it.
right: The man who lives here. The book that I read.

name: Вежливая просьба — would like (+ to + глагол)
text_ru: Вежливая просьба — I would like (I'd like) a coffee; перед глаголом — would like to: I would like to go.
text_en: For polite requests use would like (I'd like a coffee), and would like to before a verb (I would like to go).
wrong: I like a coffee, please. I would like go there.
right: I would like a coffee, please. I would like to go there.

name: Как выполняется действие — наречие (-ly, well, fast, hard)
text_ru: Чтобы описать, как выполняется действие, нужно наречие: обычно прилагательное + -ly (carefully), но good — well, fast — fast, hard — hard.
text_en: To describe how something is done use an adverb: usually adjective + -ly (carefully), but good — well, fast — fast, hard — hard.
wrong: He drives careful and speaks English good.
right: He drives carefully and speaks English well.

name: Условные 1-го и 2-го типа: после if — без will / would (If I have..., If I had...)
text_en: After if do not use will or would: first conditional if + Present Simple (If I have time), second conditional if + Past Simple (If I had money).
wrong: If I will have time, I will call. If I would have money, I would travel.
right: If I have time, I will call. If I had money, I would travel.

name: Главная часть: 1-й тип — will, 2-й — would
text_en: In the result clause use will for a real possibility and would for an imaginary situation: If I had money, I would buy a car.
wrong: If I had money, I will buy a car.
right: If I had money, I would buy a car.

name: unless / until уже значат «если не» / «пока не» — not не нужен
text_en: Unless already means if not and until means up to the time when, so do not add another negative: Unless you hurry...; until you come.
wrong: Unless you don't hurry, you will be late. I won't leave until you won't come.
right: Unless you hurry, you will be late. I won't leave until you come.

name: know, want, understand, like, have (иметь) — без Continuous
text_en: State verbs (know, want, understand, like, have meaning own) are not normally used in Continuous tenses: I know the answer; I have a car.
wrong: I am knowing the answer. I am having a car.
right: I know the answer. I have a car.

name: used to — только о прошлом; did + use to; о настоящем — usually
text_en: Used to describes past habits and states only; after did use use to (I didn't use to), and for present habits use usually.
wrong: I didn't used to like it. I use to get up early now.
right: I didn't use to like it. I usually get up early now.

name: be / get used to + -ing (привыкнуть)
text_en: Be / get used to means be / become accustomed to and is followed by the -ing form: I am used to getting up early.
wrong: I am used to get up early. I can't used to it.
right: I am used to getting up early. I can't get used to it.

name: tell + кто-то, say — без; просьба — told me (not) to
text_en: Tell needs a person after it (He told me), say does not (He said that / said to me); for reported orders use tell someone (not) to do.
wrong: He said me that he was tired. He told me don't go.
right: He told me that he was tired. He told me not to go.

name: Косвенный вопрос: прямой порядок слов, if для общих вопросов
text_en: In reported and polite indirect questions use statement word order, and if / whether for yes-no questions: She asked where I lived; Could you tell me what your strengths are?
wrong: She asked where do I live. He asked do I like coffee.
right: She asked where I lived. He asked if I liked coffee.

name: После глагола в прошедшем — сдвиг времени: is → was, will → would
text_en: After a past reporting verb the tense usually moves back: is becomes was, will becomes would.
wrong: She said she is tired. I knew he will come.
right: She said she was tired. I knew he would come.

name: Предположение: must — уверен, что да; can't — уверен, что нет; might — возможно
text_en: For deductions use must when you are sure something is true, can't when you are sure it is not, and might / could when it is possible.
wrong: The lights are off. He mustn't be at home.
right: The lights are off. He can't be at home.

name: be able to там, где can не может: will be able, have been able, was able (удалось)
text_en: Can has no future or perfect forms, so use will be able to and have been able to; for one success in the past use was able to.
wrong: I will can help you. I have can't sleep.
right: I will be able to help you. I haven't been able to sleep.

name: Разделительный вопрос: тот же вспомогательный глагол, противоположный знак
text_en: A question tag repeats the auxiliary of the sentence with the opposite polarity: You like tea, don't you? She is nice, isn't she?
wrong: You like tea, isn't it? She is nice, is she?
right: You like tea, don't you? She is nice, isn't she?

name: had + третья форма — действие раньше другого в прошлом
text_en: Use had + past participle for an action that happened before another past action: When I arrived, the train had already left.
wrong: When I arrived, the train already left.
right: When I arrived, the train had already left.

name: have / has been + глагол с -ing
text_en: The Present Perfect Continuous is have / has been + verb-ing: I have been working; she has been waiting.
wrong: I have working here. She have been waiting.
right: I have been working here. She has been waiting.

name: Действие длится до сих пор (for, since, How long) — Present Perfect Continuous
text_en: For an activity that started in the past and is still going on, especially with for, since and How long, use the Present Perfect Continuous: I have been working here since 2020.
wrong: I work here since 2020. How long are you waiting?
right: I have been working here since 2020. How long have you been waiting?

name: be + третья форма; исполнитель — by; I was born
text_en: The passive is be + past participle, with by for the doer; to be born is always passive: I was born in 2004.
wrong: The report written by the team. I born in 2004. The house was build.
right: The report was written by the team. I was born in 2004. The house was built.

name: happen, die, arrive, appear не бывают в пассиве
text_en: Verbs without an object (happen, die, arrive, appear) cannot be passive: The accident happened.
wrong: The accident was happened yesterday.
right: The accident happened yesterday.

name: Сложные случаи: go to school / bed, реки и озёра, абстрактные понятия
text_en: Use no article with places used for their purpose (go to school, go to bed) and abstract nouns in general (Nature is beautiful); rivers and seas take the, lakes and single mountains do not.
wrong: He goes to the school. The nature is beautiful.
right: He goes to school. Nature is beautiful.

name: few / little — мало (плохо), a few / a little — немного (хорошо)
text_en: Few / little mean not many / not much (negative); a few / a little mean some (positive).
wrong: I have few friends, so I'm never lonely.
right: I have a few friends, so I'm never lonely.

name: every + ед. ч.; most без of; neither вместо both... not; no / none of
text_en: Every takes a singular noun and verb; say most people, not most of people; use neither instead of both... not; use no + noun but none of + the / a pronoun.
wrong: I go there every days. Most of people like it. Both of them don't like it.
right: I go there every day. Most people like it. Neither of them likes it.

name: 3-й тип — только о прошлом: if + had + третья форма, would have + третья форма
text_en: For imaginary past situations use if + had + past participle and would have + past participle: If I had known, I would have come.
wrong: If I would have known, I would come.
right: If I had known, I would have come.

name: Условие в прошлом, результат сейчас — would + глагол
text_en: When a past condition has a present result, use if + had + past participle and would + base verb: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
wrong: If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor now.
right: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.

name: The more..., the more... (калька «чем больше, тем...»)
text_en: To show that two things change together use the + comparative, the + comparative: The more you read, the more you know.
wrong: More you read, more you know.
right: The more you read, the more you know.

name: Результат, количество, статичные глаголы — Perfect; длительность — Continuous
text_en: Use the Present Perfect for results, numbers of completed things and state verbs, and the Present Perfect Continuous for the duration of an activity.
wrong: I have been writing three letters. I have been knowing him for years.
right: I have written three letters. I have known him for years.

name: Рассказ о прошлом: фон — Past Continuous, без переключения на настоящее
text_en: In a story keep to past tenses: Past Simple for the main events, Past Continuous for the background, Past Perfect for earlier events.
wrong: Yesterday I go to the shop and I saw my friend.
right: Yesterday I went to the shop and I saw my friend.

name: После when, as soon as, before, after, until (не if) — настоящее время, без will
text_en: After when, as soon as, before, after and until use a present tense, not will: When I finish, I will call you.
wrong: When I will finish, I will call you.
right: When I finish, I will call you.

name: Future Continuous — будет в процессе; Future Perfect — будет сделано к...
text_en: Use will be + -ing for an action in progress at a future time and will have + past participle for an action completed by a future time.
wrong: This time tomorrow I will lie on the beach. By 2030 I will finish university.
right: This time tomorrow I will be lying on the beach. By 2030 I will have finished university.

name: После wish — сдвиг назад: Past Simple о настоящем, Past Perfect о прошлом, could об умении
text_en: After wish move the tense back: Past Simple for present wishes (I wish I had), Past Perfect for past regrets (I wish I hadn't said), could for abilities.
wrong: I wish I have more time. I wish I didn't say it yesterday.
right: I wish I had more time. I wish I hadn't said it yesterday.

name: wish + would — только о других людях, не о себе
text_en: Use wish + would to complain about other people's behaviour, not about yourself: I wish I were taller.
wrong: I wish I would be taller.
right: I wish I were taller.

name: Модальный + have + третья форма: should have, must have, can't have
text_en: Use modal + have + past participle about the past: should have for regrets, must have when you are sure it happened, can't have when you are sure it did not.
wrong: I should told you. He must have went. She mustn't have seen it.
right: I should have told you. He must have gone. She can't have seen it.

name: look / sound / taste + прилагательное, look like + существительное; can hear / see
text_en: Look, sound, smell, taste and feel take an adjective (tastes good) or like + noun (looks like a cat); for involuntary perception use can hear / can see.
wrong: This soup tastes well. You look like tired. I am hearing music.
right: This soup tastes good. You look tired. I can hear music.

name: Пассив с модальными, Continuous и Perfect: must be done, is being built, has been done
text_en: Complex passive forms keep be: modal + be + participle (must be done), is being + participle, has been + participle.
wrong: It must done today. The house is building now.
right: It must be done today. The house is being built now.

name: Услугу делает кто-то другой — have something done
text_en: When someone else does a service for you, use have + object + past participle: I had my hair cut.
wrong: I cut my hair at the hairdresser's yesterday.
right: I had my hair cut at the hairdresser's yesterday.

name: had been + -ing — действие длилось до момента в прошлом
text_en: Use had been + -ing for an activity that continued up to a moment in the past: She had been crying for an hour when I came.
wrong: She was crying for an hour when I came.
right: She had been crying for an hour when I came.

name: Ошибка в написании слова (receive, friend, beautiful)
text_ru: Слово написано с ошибкой — проверьте, как оно пишется (receive, friend, beautiful). И помните: I («я») всегда пишется с заглавной буквы.
text_en: The word is misspelled — check how it is written (receive, friend, beautiful). Remember that I is always a capital letter.
wrong: I recieve letters from my freind.
right: I receive letters from my friend.

name: Не то слово или неверное сочетание (make / do, learn / teach)
text_ru: Слова сочетаются устойчивыми парами (take a photo, make a mistake), а дословный перевод часто даёт не то слово (learn — учиться самому, teach — учить кого-то).
text_en: Some words go together in fixed pairs (take a photo, make a mistake), and a literal translation often gives the wrong word (learn vs teach).
wrong: I made a photo. I want to learn you English.
right: I took a photo. I want to teach you English.

name: Предлог в паре со словом (interested in, good at, depend on)
text_ru: Предлог запоминают вместе со словом (interested in, good at, depend on); дословный перевод с русского часто неверен.
text_en: Prepositions are learned together with the word (interested in, good at, depend on); a literal translation from Russian is often wrong.
wrong: I am good in planning and depend from my parents.
right: I am good at planning and depend on my parents.

name: Порядок слов: прилагательное перед существительным, наречие не между глаголом и дополнением
text_ru: Прилагательное стоит перед существительным (a red car), а наречие не ставится между глаголом и дополнением (I like it very much).
text_en: Adjectives go before the noun (a red car), and an adverb does not come between the verb and its object (I like it very much).
wrong: I have a car red. I like very much it.
right: I have a red car. I like it very much.

name: Одно отрицание в предложении (never, nothing, nobody уже отрицательные)
text_ru: В английском предложении одно отрицание: never, nothing, nobody уже отрицательные, поэтому not с ними не нужен (I know nothing / I don't know anything).
text_en: An English sentence has only one negative: never, nothing and nobody are already negative (I know nothing / I don't know anything).
wrong: I don't know nothing. I don't never eat meat.
right: I don't know anything. I never eat meat.

name: Ошибка не подходит ни под одно правило
